title: Negative: CGLE pulses on a depletable gain medium in a 4x larger box keep a fragmenting worm population (eps 1.43) or a static crescent population (eps 1.4), but daughters do not persist and the crescents do not swim
summary: world.py of 20261026T1530-c43-cgle-gain-sighting at L=80, 192^2 (same dx), seed 2, t=1000, eps 1.40/1.42/1.43/1.45. eps 1.40: 10-16 comma pulses each in a gain-depletion halo; they do not swim (motion.py: 0 of 34 tracks reach 3 body lengths, best 0.4-0.9 over 200-320 t) and their number falls by merges (persistent splits 0, merge/split 1.5). eps 1.42: commas plus one spinning vortex-ring pulse with a dark phase-singular core that persists t=260-1000. eps 1.43: a standing population of worms that grow, writhe and fragment while fragments regrow into worms (sheet t=480-1000), but labkit counts 16 splits, 1 persistent, 15 merges: the pieces re-merge or fade within 100 t. eps 1.45: a domain wall wraps the box, with ring pulses and short-lived worms. Depletion of a regrowing gain medium turns c03's static pulses into growing and breaking worms, but in this scan it never produces persistent daughters.

finding.operator: depletable regrowing gain medium under a cubic-quintic CGLE field
finding.control: eps scan at fixed medium, one seed; tracker motion.py for M
finding.result: persistent splits 0/0/1/1 at eps 1.40/1.42/1.43/1.45 (merges 15/16/15/12); 0/34 crescent tracks >= 3 body lengths at eps 1.40

limits: One seed per setting, t=1000, one gain medium setting (sig 0.05, gam 0.02, Dg 0.5, g0 0.9). The labkit lineage window is 100 t; I did not re-run it with a shorter window. A worm regime with slower gain recovery or a real repulsion between pieces (nu, D) is untested.
